reason: The Hebrew text contains multiple instances of the Israelites voicing criticism against their leaders, Moses and Aaron. Notable examples include: 'וַיִּלֹּ֧נוּ כָּל־ עֲדַ֧ת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עַל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְעַֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן בַּמִּדְבָּֽר' (the whole congregation of the children of Israel complained against Moses and Aaron); complaints about lack of water ('תְּנוּ־ לָ֥נוּ מַ֖יִם'); accusations that Moses brought them out to die in the wilderness ('לָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ הֶעֱלִיתָ֣נוּ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לְהָמִ֥ית אֹתִ֛י'); and sarcastic criticism ('חֲדַ֥ל מִמֶּ֖נּוּ וְנַֽעַבְדָ֣ה אֶת־ מִצְרָ֑יִם'). These complaints are directed at their leaders' decisions and God's actions in delivering them to the wilderness.
